chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about a woman who donated her wealth to the poor, if she went out with her husband, then she went out with him, he said: 'There is no obligation upon her.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهَا شَيْءٌ: There is no obligation/penalty upon her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman donating her wealth to the poor without her husband's permission?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the validity of a woman's independent charity (*sadaqah*) from her own wealth, ruling that it remains binding even if she later accompanies her husband, thereby affirming her financial autonomy in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores that her donation does not require spousal consent to be valid, distinguishing it from other forms of expenditure that might necessitate permission. The context highlights the practical application of property rights for women in the early Shia legal tradition.
